questoes.pergunta: What requirement must the schema meet in order to use strict: true?
opcoes: Have at least one field of type string
additionalProperties: false on every object
Use only numeric types
Declare minimum and maximum on every numeric field in the schema
questoes.explicacao: Strict requires closed objects (additionalProperties: false). Optional properties are allowed but count toward a limit; the recommendation is required + nullable.
feedbacks: Incorrect: there's no type requirement.
Correct.
Incorrect: any basic type is supported.
Incorrect: numeric ranges aren't even guaranteed by strict.

questoes.pergunta: Customer Support scenario: the system prompt says 'never grant a discount above 15%'. In 1 out of every 200 conversations, the agent grants 20%. The team has already rewritten the instruction twice, with examples. What is the fix?
opcoes: Add more examples of discount refusals
Repeat the rule at the beginning and at the end of the system prompt
Ask the agent to confirm the amount with the customer first
Validate the percentage in code (a hook before apply_discount) and block anything above 15%
questoes.explicacao: A critical financial rule goes into deterministic code; a prompt has a nonzero failure rate.
feedbacks: More prompt; still probabilistic.
Repetition helps little and guarantees nothing.
The customer is not the policy control.
Correct.

questoes.pergunta: A moderation pipeline processes user-submitted texts. In some cases the API returns HTTP 200, but content doesn't contain the expected classification and the pipeline records 'no violation'. What is the likely cause and the fix?
opcoes: Intermittent network timeout; add retry with exponential backoff and jitter
Ambiguous prompt; add few-shot
Refusal: check stop_reason == refusal before reading content
Low max_tokens; raise the limit
questoes.explicacao: A refusal arrives with HTTP 200 and stop_reason refusal; code that ignores stop_reason treats it as an empty success.
feedbacks: A timeout doesn't come back as HTTP 200.
Few-shot doesn't change the fact that the pipeline records a result without checking why generation stopped.
Correct: check stop_reason before consuming content.
Truncation would leave partial output, not missing output; and the symptom 'HTTP 200 with no useful content' points to refusal.

questoes.pergunta: Which statement about the Batch API is correct?
opcoes: It guarantees a response within 1 hour
It returns results in the same order as the requests
It supports a multi-turn tool loop within a request
~50% cheaper, up to 24h, no SLA
questoes.explicacao: 50% discount, up to 24h, no SLA; results come back out of order; no multi-turn tool use.
feedbacks: Incorrect: there's no SLA; it can take up to 24h.
Incorrect: out of order → match by custom_id.
Incorrect: each request is a single call.
Correct.

questoes.pergunta: Structured Data Extraction scenario: a pipeline asks the model to 'respond only with JSON' and parses the response. On 4% of documents the parse fails because there is text before the JSON or a field is missing. What is the BEST fix?
opcoes: Use structured outputs (output_config.format with the extraction's JSON schema)
Extract the JSON with a regex that looks for the first '{' and the last '}'
Repeat the instruction 'ONLY JSON' at the beginning and at the end of the prompt
Prefill the assistant turn with '{'
questoes.explicacao: Structured outputs guarantees a response that conforms to the schema; the other options are patches or are invalid on newer models.
feedbacks: Correct.
A fragile patch: it handles the surrounding text, not the missing field.
Emphasis gives no structural guarantee.
Prefill returns 400 on newer models and doesn't guarantee the schema.

questoes.pergunta: Code Generation scenario: a PM asks for 'a configurable delinquency report'. The period, the filters, the export format, and who has access are all unclear. What should you ask Claude Code to do first?
opcoes: Implement the most complete version possible, with every option
Ask about the open points before coding
Implement the minimal version and wait for feedback in production
Write the user documentation first
questoes.explicacao: Interview: with a fuzzy requirement, the questions surface hidden assumptions before any code is written.
feedbacks: Spends effort on possibly wrong assumptions.
Correct.
Discovers the wrong assumptions late, and in production.
Documenting without deciding the rules doesn't resolve the open questions.

questoes.pergunta: A fintech has a support agent (Agent SDK) that can call process_refund. The policy says refunds above $500 require human approval. In an audit, 3% of the refunds above the limit were processed without approval, despite an ALL-CAPS instruction in the system prompt. What is the BEST fix?
opcoes: Rewrite the instruction with few-shot examples of denied refunds
Add a second model that reviews each refund and vetoes those that violate the policy before execution
Block process_refund above $500 with a hook in code
Reduce the agent's number of tools so it pays more attention to the rule
questoes.explicacao: A rule with financial consequences requires deterministic enforcement. A prompt (even with few-shot) has a nonzero failure rate.
feedbacks: Tempting because few-shot improves adherence, but it is still probabilistic: it reduces the 3%, it doesn't eliminate it.
Tempting because it looks like a 'double check', but it is more complex and also probabilistic; the tiebreaker favors deterministic code.
Correct: a hook/validation enforces the rule in 100% of cases.
Too many tools is a real anti-pattern, but it isn't the cause here; the critical rule lives only in the prompt.

questoes.pergunta: Which retry message is the most effective in a validation loop?
opcoes: 'The JSON is invalid. Try again.'
'Review your answer more carefully and check every field before responding.'
'Error 422.'
'total 1250.00 ≠ sum of items 1205.00 (item 3?)'
questoes.explicacao: Specific errors (what and where) give the model something to fix.
feedbacks: Incorrect: generic; it tends to produce the same response.
Incorrect: vague.
Incorrect: a code with no context (the generic-error anti-pattern).
Correct.
